Chart of Barcelona's league performance 1929–2023

On 7 March 2021, Joan Laporta was elected president of Barcelona with 54.28% of the vote.[[172]](#cite_note-172) Barcelona won their 31st Copa del Rey, their only trophy under Ronald Koeman, after defeating Athletic Bilbao 4–0 in the [final](/wiki/2021_Copa_del_Rey_Final "2021 Copa del Rey Final").[[173]](#cite_note-173) In August 2021, Barcelona found themselves unable to comply with La Liga's Financial Fair Play requirements, and revealed a club debt of €1.35bn and a wage bill accounting for 103% of total income. Negotiations with Lionel Messi, now in the final year of his contract, had been ongoing for some time. However, on 5 August 2021, Barcelona announced that they would be unable to re-sign Messi to an extension due to La Liga regulations. This was despite the fact that the club and Messi had reached an agreement over the details of a new contract. Messi departed the club after 21 years as a Barça player, and the club's all-time leading goalscorer, and signed on a free transfer with French club [Paris Saint-Germain](/wiki/Paris_Saint-Germain "Paris Saint-Germain").[[174]](#cite_note-174)[[175]](#cite_note-175) The financial implications also restricted Barcelona in the transfer market and as a result most of the incoming players were either free transfers or loans and they had to reduce players' wages to register the incoming players.[[176]](#cite_note-176)

Poor performances in [La Liga](/wiki/2021%E2%80%9322_La_Liga "2021–22 La Liga") and the [Champions League](/wiki/2021%E2%80%9322_UEFA_Champions_League "2021–22 UEFA Champions League") led to the sacking of Ronald Koeman on 28 October, with a club legend [Xavi](/wiki/Xavi_(footballer,_born_1980) "Xavi (footballer, born 1980)") replacing him.[[177]](#cite_note-177)[[178]](#cite_note-178) Xavi cou

Main article: [Older Parthenon](/wiki/Older_Parthenon "Older Parthenon")

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/95/Parthenon_ancient_%26_Pericles%2C_Maxime_Collignon.jpg/250px-Parthenon_ancient_%26_Pericles%2C_Maxime_Collignon.jpg)](/wiki/File:Parthenon_ancient_%26_Pericles,_Maxime_Collignon.jpg)

The [Older Parthenon](/wiki/Older_Parthenon "Older Parthenon") (in black) was destroyed by the Achaemenids during the [Destruction of Athens](/wiki/Destruction_of_Athens "Destruction of Athens") in 480–479 BC, and then rebuilt by [Pericles](/wiki/Pericles "Pericles") (in grey).

The first endeavour to build a sanctuary for [Athena Parthenos](/wiki/Athena#Athena_Parthenos:_Virgin_Athena "Athena") on the site of the present Parthenon was begun shortly after the [Battle of Marathon](/wiki/Battle_of_Marathon "Battle of Marathon") (c. 490–488 BC) upon a solid [limestone](/wiki/Limestone "Limestone") foundation that extended and levelled the southern part of the [Acropolis](/wiki/Acropolis "Acropolis") summit. This building replaced a [Hekatompedon temple](/wiki/Hekatompedon_temple "Hekatompedon temple") ("hundred-footer") and would have stood beside the [archaic temple dedicated to *Athena Polias*](/wiki/Old_Temple_of_Athena "Old Temple of Athena") ("of the city"). The [Older or Pre-Parthenon](/wiki/Older_Parthenon "Older Parthenon"), as it is frequently called, was still under construction when the [Persians](/wiki/Achaemenid_Empire "Achaemenid Empire") sacked the city in 480 BC and razed the Acropolis.[[51]](#cite_note-venieri-acropolis-51)[[52]](#cite_note-52)

The existence of both the proto-Parthenon and its destruction were known from [Herodotus](/wiki/Herodotus "Herodotus"),[[53]](#cite_note-53) and the drums of its columns were visibly built into the curtain wall north of the [Erechtheion](/wiki/Erechtheion "Erechtheion"). Further physical evidence of this structure was revealed with the excavations of [Panagiotis Kavvadias](/wiki/Panagiotis_Kavvadias "Panagiotis Kavvadias") of 1885–1890. YouTube :: History :: "Broadcast Yourself" era (2006–2013) :: chunk_0004
On October 9, 2006, [Google](/wiki/Google "Google") announced that they had acquired YouTube for $1.65 billion in Google stock.[[42]](#cite_note-42)[[43]](#cite_note-43) The deal was finalized on November 13, 2006.[[44]](#cite_note-44)[[45]](#cite_note-45) Google's acquisition launched newfound interest in video-sharing sites; [IAC](/wiki/IAC_(company) "IAC (company)"), which now owned [Vimeo](/wiki/Vimeo "Vimeo"), focused on supporting the content creators to distinguish itself from YouTube.[[33]](#cite_note-fortune_vimeo-33) It was at this time that YouTube adopted the slogan "Broadcast Yourself".
The company experienced rapid growth. *[The Daily Telegraph](/wiki/The_Daily_Telegraph "The Daily Telegraph")* wrote that in 2007, YouTube consumed as much [bandwidth](/wiki/Bandwidth_(computing) "Bandwidth (computing)") as the entire Internet in 2000.[[46]](#cite_note-46) By 2010, the company had reached a [market share](/wiki/Market_share "Market share") of around 43% and more than 14 billion views of videos, according to [comScore](/wiki/ComScore "ComScore").[[47]](#cite_note-47) That year, the company simplified its interface to increase the time users would spend on the site.[[48]](#cite_note-48)

In 2011, more than three billion videos were being watched each day with 48 hours of new videos uploaded every minute.[[49]](#cite_note-49)[[50]](#cite_note-50)[[51]](#cite_note-51) Most of these views came from a relatively small number of videos; according to a software engineer at that time, 30% of videos accounted for 99% of views on the site.[[52]](#cite_note-52) That year, the company again changed its interface and at the same time, introduced a new logo with a darker shade of red.[[53]](#cite_note-53)[[54]](#cite_note-54) A subsequent interface change, designed to unify the experience across desktop, TV, and mobile, was rolled out in 2013.[[55]](#cite_note-55) By that point, more than 100 hours were being uploaded every minute, increasing to 300 hours by November 2014.[[56]](#cite_note-56)[[57]](#cite_note-57)

Itaipu Dam :: part 02 :: chunk_0001
With its construction completed in 1984, it is a binational undertaking run by Brazil and Paraguay at the border between the two countries, 15 km (9.3 mi) north of the [Friendship Bridge](/wiki/Friendship_Bridge_(Paraguay%E2%80%93Brazil) "Friendship Bridge (Paraguay–Brazil)"). The project ranges from [Foz do Iguaçu](/wiki/Foz_do_Igua%C3%A7u "Foz do Iguaçu"), in Brazil, and [Ciudad del Este](/wiki/Ciudad_del_Este "Ciudad del Este") in Paraguay, in the south to [Guaíra](/wiki/Gua%C3%ADra,_Paran%C3%A1 "Guaíra, Paraná") and [Salto del Guairá](/wiki/Salto_del_Guair%C3%A1 "Salto del Guairá") in the north. The installed generation capacity of the plant is 14 GW, with 20 generating units providing 700 MW each with a hydraulic design head of 118 metres (387 ft). In 2016, the plant employed 3038 workers.[[3]](#cite_note-3)

Of the twenty generator units currently installed, ten generate at 50 [Hz](/wiki/Hertz "Hertz") for Paraguay and ten generate at 60 Hz for Brazil. Since the output capacity of the Paraguayan generators far exceeds the load in Paraguay, most of their production is exported directly to the Brazilian side, from where two [600 kV HVDC](/wiki/HVDC_Itaipu "HVDC Itaipu") lines, each approximately 800 kilometres (500 mi) long, carry the majority of the energy to the [São Paulo](/wiki/S%C3%A3o_Paulo "São Paulo")/[Rio de Janeiro](/wiki/Rio_de_Janeiro "Rio de Janeiro") region where the terminal equipment converts the power to 60 Hz.

Messi's success on the pitch has earned him lucrative endorsement deals along with widespread recognition and popularity.

Messi was among the [*Time* 100](/wiki/Time_100 "Time 100"), an annual list of the world's most influential people, in 2011, 2012 and 2023.[[W]](#cite_note-340) According to a 2014 survey in 15 international markets, Messi was familiar to 87% of respondents around the world, of whom 78% perceived him favourably, making him the second-most recognised player globally, behind [Cristiano Ronaldo](/wiki/Cristiano_Ronaldo "Cristiano Ronaldo"), and the most likeable of all contemporary players.[[314]](#cite_note-341)[[315]](#cite_note-342) [World Press Photo](/wiki/World_Press_Photo "World Press Photo") selected "The Final Game", a photo of Messi facing the [World Cup trophy](/wiki/FIFA_World_Cup_Trophy "FIFA World Cup Trophy") after Argentina's final defeat to Germany, as the best sports image of 2014.[[316]](#cite_note-343)

Messi's fanbase on [Facebook](/wiki/Facebook "Facebook") is among the largest of public figures: by July 2023, he had [more than 114 million followers](/wiki/List_of_most-followed_Facebook_pages "List of most-followed Facebook pages"), the second highest for an athlete after Cristiano Ronaldo.[[317]](#cite_note-344)[[318]](#cite_note-345) Messi has over 500 million [Instagram](/wiki/Instagram "Instagram") followers, the [second highest for an individual](/wiki/List_of_most-followed_Instagram_accounts "List of most-followed Instagram accounts") and athlete after Ronaldo.[[319]](#cite_note-346) Messi's World Cup celebration post from 18 December 2022 is the [most liked post on Instagram](/wiki/List_of_most-liked_Instagram_posts "List of most-liked Instagram posts") with more than 75 million likes.[[320]](#cite_note-347) In April 2023, Messi was featured in the [Thrissur Pooram](/wiki/Thrissur_Pooram "Thrissur Pooram") festival in [Kerala](/wiki/Kerala "Kerala"), India.[[321]](#cite_note-348)[[32

Main article: [Seattle SuperSonics](/wiki/Seattle_SuperSonics "Seattle SuperSonics")

The Thunder's previous incarnation, the [Seattle SuperSonics](/wiki/Seattle_SuperSonics "Seattle SuperSonics"), were formed in 1967. In their 41 seasons in [Seattle](/wiki/Seattle "Seattle"), the SuperSonics compiled a 1,745–1,585 (.524) win–loss record in the regular season and went 107–110 (.493) in the playoffs. The franchise's titles include three [Western Conference](/wiki/Western_Conference_(NBA) "Western Conference (NBA)") championships (1978, 1979 and 1996) and one [NBA title](/wiki/NBA_Finals "NBA Finals") in [1979](/wiki/1979_NBA_Finals "1979 NBA Finals"). In their last season, they drafted franchise player [Kevin Durant](/wiki/Kevin_Durant "Kevin Durant"), setting up the Thunder for success.

Brooklyn Latin

Main article: [Brooklyn Latin School](/wiki/Brooklyn_Latin_School "Brooklyn Latin School")

Unlike nearly all other specialized high schools, Brooklyn Latin has a strong focus on the humanities and classics. All students are required to take four years of English, History, Latin, and a modern foreign language. All classes regularly hold Socratic Seminars, in which students lead roundtable question-and-answer discussions, and all students take part in declamation (public speaking) exercises. Because of its small class size, Brooklyn Latin offers a relatively low student-to-teacher ratio (currently around 16:1). All students are required to take [International Baccalaureate](/wiki/International_Baccalaureate "International Baccalaureate") courses in junior and senior years.

fanoutqa_036375.t: List of tallest trees :: Maximum limits of tree height :: chunk_0003
fanoutqa_036375.x:
List of tallest trees :: Maximum limits of tree height :: chunk_0003
Two main opposing forces affect a [tree](/wiki/Tree "Tree")'s height; one pushes it upward while the other holds it down. By analyzing the interplay between these forces in coast redwoods (*Sequoia sempervirens*), a team of biologists led by George Koch of [Northern Arizona University](/wiki/Northern_Arizona_University "Northern Arizona University") calculated the theoretical maximum tree height or the point at which opposing forces balance out and a tree stops growing. This point lies somewhere between 122 and 130 m (400 and 427 ft).[[51]](#cite_note-52) On the one hand, the researchers found, trees in forests "desire" to grow as tall as possible to overtake neighboring trees and reach stronger sunlight. On the other hand, gravity makes it more and more difficult to haul water upwards from the roots to the [canopy](/wiki/Canopy_(biology) "Canopy (biology)") as the tree grows, and [leaves](/wiki/Leaf "Leaf") thus become smaller near the top. They discovered that despite the moistness of the ground far below, the leaves at the treetops struggle to get enough water, so they are effectively living in a constant drought. The difficulty of getting [water](/wiki/Water "Water") so far up into the sky is what ultimately constrains growth.[[52]](#cite_note-53) Other researchers have developed models of maximum height for Coast Douglas-fir (*Pseudotsuga menziesii var. menziesii*) trees that yield similar estimates of 109 to 138 meters (358 to 453 ft),[[53]](#cite_note-:1-54) a range that includes the height of the tallest reliably-measured historical (dead) specimen, a 126-meter tree.[[53]](#cite_note-:1-54)[[54]](#cite_note-55)[[55]](#cite_note-56)

**Sir Lewis Carl Davidson Hamilton** (born 7 January 1985) is a British [racing driver](/wiki/Racing_driver "Racing driver") who competes in [Formula One](/wiki/Formula_One "Formula One") for [Ferrari](/wiki/Scuderia_Ferrari "Scuderia Ferrari"). Hamilton has won a joint-record seven [Formula One World Drivers' Championship titles](/wiki/Formula_One_World_Drivers%27_Championship_titles "Formula One World Drivers' Championship titles")—tied with [Michael Schumacher](/wiki/Michael_Schumacher "Michael Schumacher")—and holds the [records](/wiki/List_of_Formula_One_driver_records "List of Formula One driver records") for most [wins](/wiki/List_of_Formula_One_Grand_Prix_winners "List of Formula One Grand Prix winners") (105), [pole positions](/wiki/List_of_Formula_One_polesitters "List of Formula One polesitters") (104), and [podium finishes](/wiki/List_of_Formula_One_driver_records#Total_podium_finishes "List of Formula One driver records") (203), among [others](/wiki/List_of_career_achievements_by_Lewis_Hamilton#Records "List of career achievements by Lewis Hamilton").

Born and raised in [Stevenage](/wiki/Stevenage "Stevenage"), Hamilton began his career in [karting](/wiki/Kart_racing "Kart racing") at age six, winning several national titles and attracting the attention of [Ron Dennis](/wiki/Ron_Dennis "Ron Dennis"), who signed him to the [McLaren-Mercedes Young Driver Programme](/wiki/McLaren_Young_Driver_Programme "McLaren Young Driver Programme") in 1998. After winning the [Karting World Cup](/wiki/Karting_World_Cup "Karting World Cup") and [European Championship](/wiki/Karting_European_Championship "Karting European Championship") in 2000, Hamilton progressed to [junior formulae](/wiki/Formula_racing "Formula racing"), where his successes included winning the [Formula 3 Euro Series](/wiki/2005_Formula_3_Euro_Series "2005 Formula 3 Euro Series") and the [GP2 Series](/wiki/2006_GP2_Series "2006 GP2 Series").
